works.title: Dual Regulation of Monomer Transport Enables Ultrahigh Mg2+/Li+ Selectivity in Polyamide Nanofiltration Membranes
institutions: University of Science and Technology of China , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Nanofiltration membranes are promising for lithium recovery from salt-lake brines, yet their Mg2+/Li+ separation performance can be further improved. Here, we present an organic-phase engineering strategy that systematically tailors the carbon-chain length of alkane solvents, from n-hexane (C6) to 2-methylundecane (C12), to simultaneously regulate piperazine enrichment at the water–organic interface and trimesoyl chloride diffusion kinetics. This dual regulation transforms conventional rapid and random interfacial polymerization into a more confined and homogeneous growth process. The resulting polyamide membranes exhibit a reduced negative surface charge and a narrower and more uniform pore-size distribution. These structural features substantially enhance Mg2+/Li+ separation, with the C12 membrane achieving a Mg2+/Li+ selectivity of up to 306.6 in the mixed-salt solutions. To assess performance under realistic conditions, a two-pass nanofiltration process was evaluated using simulated salt-lake brine. The C12 membrane increased lithium purity from 2.4% to 97.7% while reducing the Mg2+/Li+ mass ratio from 40 to 0.024. This study provides new insight into the kinetic regulation of interfacial polymerization through organic-phase engineering and demonstrates an effective membrane design strategy for high-selectivity lithium extraction from complex brines.

works.title: High-flux dual-charged composite nanofiltration membranes with electrical double layer architectures for efficient low-pressure water purification
works.journal: Frontiers in Membrane Science and Technology
institutions: Zhejiang Mey Membrane Technology Co.,Ltd, Xindeng
works.abstract: Traditional thin-film composite (TFC) nanofiltration (NF) membranes are constrained by a permeability–selectivity trade-off arising from limited surface charge density and high hydraulic resistance contributed by non-woven fabric backing layers. Here we report high-flux composite Nanofiltration membranes engineered with a dual electrical double layer (EDL) architecture that integrates charged functional groups into both the porous support and the ultrathin selective layer. Strongly negatively charged membranes based on sulfonated polyvinylidene fluoride or sulfonated polyethersulfone achieved multivalent salt rejections of 95.6%–99.3% while delivering pure-water permeances up to approximately 37 L m -2 h -1 bar -1 . Non-woven-free variants maintained stable, high-efficiency removal of multivalent salts, heavy-metal ions (Pb 2+ ), viruses, and bacteria under ultra-low operating pressures (≤0.1 MPa). Zeta-potential measurements confirmed that the dual-charged EDL structures sustain high-magnitude, pH-invariant surface potentials across the range pH 1–13. These membranes enable pump-free household filtration, municipal water treatment, wastewater reclamation, and decentralized rural water supply, directly addressing the need for energy-efficient, high-selectivity water purification technologies.

works.title: Spirobisindane‐Based Microporous Nanofilms With Tunable Network for Precise Molecular Sieving
institutions: University of Science and Technology of China

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Manipulating polymer network architecture is critical to advancing organic solvent nanofiltration (OSN) membranes. Here we report a pH‐regulated interfacial polymerization strategy that employs rigid spirobisindane (SBI) monomers bearing hydroxyl and amine functionalities. Regulating phenolic hydroxyl participation enables the same dual‐functional SBI monomer to form either an amide‐dominated or a mixed amide/ester‐linked network, while a hydroxyl‐functional SBI monomer provides an ester‐dominated reference. Spectroscopic characterization, gas sorption analysis, and molecular simulations collectively reveal how network chemistry and packing regulate free‐volume organization and pore‐size distributions, thereby controlling solvent transport and molecular sieving. The mixed amide/ester‐linked SBI‐NH 2 ‐OH membrane exhibits a high microporous surface area (272 m 2 g −1 ) and high methanol permeance (22.7 L m −2 h −1 bar −1 ), whereas the amide‐dominated SBI‐NH 2 membrane provides tight molecular sieving with narrow pore size distributions. In contrast, the ester‐dominated SBI‐OH membrane exhibits larger average interchain spacing and a broader pore‐size distribution, accompanied by reduced selectivity. Notably, the SBI‐derived nanofilms display good pressure stability and solvent resistance. Moreover, successful larger‐area fabrication of both SBI‐NH 2 and SBI‐NH 2 ‐OH membranes demonstrates the compatibility of the fabrication strategy with scale‐up. Taken together, these findings demonstrate pH‐regulated functional‐group participation as a molecular design strategy that translates chemical reactivity into network architecture and transport behavior, offering a rational pathway toward scalable OSN membranes for energy‐efficient separations.

works.title: Ion Valence Difference Governs Membrane Charge Preference in Nanofiltration-Based Radionuclide Separation
works.abstract: Abstract Selective separation of radionuclides with varying environmental hazards is critical for mitigating the disposal burden of high-level radioactive wastewater. Although positively charged (PC) membranes are generally considered effective for cation pair separation, the applicability of negatively charged (NC) membranes for separating cations with large valence differences remains unresolved. In this study, Ag+/Zr4+ and Ag+/Sr2+ were used as representative radionuclides with large and small valence differences, respectively, to evaluate the separation performance and underlying mechanisms of PC and NC membranes. Notably, NC membranes maintained near-complete rejection of Zr4+ while simultaneously exhibiting higher Ag+ permeability, thereby achieving superior Ag+/Zr4+ selectivity relative to PC membranes. DFT calculations and MD simulations revealed that strong ion–membrane interactions facilitated preferential partitioning of Zr4+ at the NC membrane interface, whereas differences in hydration energy governed the competitive transport of Ag+ and Zr4+. Furthermore, Zr4+ accumulated at the membrane surface induced incomplete dehydration of Ag+, reducing interfacial transport barriers and promoting Ag+ permeation. Comparative analysis of Ag+/Zr4+ and Ag+/Sr2+ systems further demonstrated that ion valence difference governs the preference of membrane charges: NC membranes are preferred for M+/M4+ separations, whereas PC membranes are preferred for M+/M2+ separations, which was further validated by Li+/Mg2+ and Li+/Ti4+ separations. These findings clarify the mechanistic distinction between co-ion and counterion competition, providing guidance for the selection of membrane charge types for energy-efficient radionuclide separation and selective resource recovery beyond the nuclear industry.

works.title: Preferential Transport of Mg2+ over Li+ in Negatively Charged Styrene Sulfonate-Regulated Graphene Oxide Nanochannels
works.abstract: Abstract Efficient lithium recovery from salt-lake brines is severely hindered by their high Mg2+/Li+ ratios. Recent nanofiltration technologies primarily directly extract lithium from brine, which incurs high energy consumption. Herein, using pressure-driven molecular dynamics simulations at 5 MPa (representative of practical operating pressures), we propose a strategy for preferential Mg2+ transport over Li+ to lower the Mg2+/Li+ mass ratios for further low-energy lithium extraction, based on intercalating styrene sulfonate inside graphene oxide nanochannels (SS–@GO). The results demonstrate a reversal in permeation selectivity from Li+ to Mg2+ upon negatively charging the lamellar channel through SS– insertion at an interlayer spacing of 1.8 nm (d). The Mg2+/Li+ selectivity exhibited a nonmonotonic dependence on negative charge density, first increasing and then decreasing, with the highest selectivity obtained at ρ = −2.07 × 10–3 e/Å2. The Mg2+/Li+ separation factor of the SS–@GO membrane can reach 16.4 at an Mg2+/Li+ mass ratio of 35. Notably, we observe that not all ions entering the channel successfully permeate, and some are reflected back to the feed side, particularly at higher negative charge densities. These findings provide molecular guidance for designing Mg2+-selective GO membrane to pretreat brines with high Mg2+/Li+ mass ratios prior to lithium recovery.

works.title: Threshold‐Voltage Ion Sieving in Ultrathin Polymeric Membranes for Energy‐Efficient Lithium Extraction
institutions: Technical Institute of Physics and Chemistry
Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

Laboratory of Bio‐Inspired Smart Interface Science, TIPC CAS Beijing China

College of Energy, Soochow Institute for Energy and Materials InnovationS (SIEMIS), Jiangsu Provincial Key Laboratory for Advanced Carbon Materials and Wearable Energy Technologies Soochow University Suzhou China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Biological ion channels achieve multi‐ion discrimination through parallel chemically distinct channel types, each optimized for a single ion species. Replicating this within a single synthetic membrane has remained beyond reach, for conventional membrane resistance blocks the bonding energy difference between different ions. Here we show that an ultrathin polymeric membrane (ca. 8.56 nm) bearing aligned angstrom‐scale porphyrin pores, fabricated by interfacial superspreading, reduces internal resistance sufficiently and achieves simultaneous multi‐ion discrimination. Under a microvolt‐scale applied voltage, the membrane separates six ion species across three valence groups. In particular, the membrane exhibits anomalous selectivity for Li + , with a threshold voltage V t ≈ 400 mV which is 370 mV above the nearest competitor. Applied to lithium extraction from low‐quality brines, a two‐stage device achieves >98% recovery at 1.1 × 10 −4 Wh g −1 (Li) , three orders of magnitude below conventional electrodialysis. This membrane architecture offers a broadly applicable design principle for energy‐intensive separations in which resolving ions of similar charge and size is the critical challenge.

works.title: pH-gated ion transport in covalent organic framework membranes functionalized with oxygen-containing groups
works.abstract: Covalent organic framework (COF) membranes with pH-gated ion transport hold promise for smart nanofluidic devices, yet the regulatory mechanisms of different oxygen-containing functional groups remain poorly understood. Herein, we systematically investigate the pH-dependent ionic conductance of TpPa-R COF membranes (R = -SO<sub>3</sub>H, -COOH, -OH) across pH 3 to 11.5 using unmodified TpPa as a reference. All membranes exhibit nanofluidic transport with a U-shaped conductance profile as a function of pH. The neutral-pH conductance is governed by the effective surface charge density that drives counterion enrichment. Among the three modifications, the TpPa-SO<sub>3</sub>H membrane displays the broadest pH response and the highest conductance at both acidic and alkaline extremes. Notably, the TpPa-COOH membrane shows unexpectedly lower conductance than TpPa-OH at pH ≥ 5, which we attribute to hydration screening that reduces the effective charge of the carboxylate groups, whereas deprotonation of the phenol groups in TpPa-OH enhances effective surface charge density and conductance at high pH. All membranes demonstrate reversible pH-switching over the tested range. This work provides a molecular-level design rationale for tailoring pH-gating performance in COF membranes and a foundation for developing tunable ion-transport devices with predictable pH responsiveness.

works.title: Influence of nanoscale effects and gradient pore-structure characteristics on the permeability of nanofiltration membranes
works.abstract: Abstract Understanding the coupled influence of nanoscale interfacial effects and pore structure is essential for clarifying water-transport mechanisms in nanofiltration (NF) membranes. Previous studies have mainly examined either nanoscale transport effects, such as wall slip and interfacial viscosity variation, or membrane structural parameters independently, while their combined effects on membrane permeability remain insufficiently understood. To address this gap, physical models of inhomogeneous, homogeneous, and gradient membrane structures were constructed, and nanopore-scale water transport was simulated using the lattice Boltzmann method while accounting for wettability-dependent slip and interfacial viscosity. The results show that, compared with the no-slip condition, nanoscale interfacial effects suppress water transport in hydrophilic membranes but substantially enhance it in hydrophobic membranes, and their influence becomes stronger as the pore size decreases. In addition, pore-size uniformity, porosity, specific interface, and membrane thickness significantly affect permeability. A characteristic factor incorporating porosity, specific interface, and thickness was proposed to describe the permeability of gradient membranes, with smaller values corresponding to higher permeability. Structural variations exert a stronger influence on hydrophobic membranes because nanoscale interfacial effects amplify the response of water transport to pore-structure changes. These results clarify the coupled roles of nanoscale interfacial transport and pore structure in NF membrane permeability and provide a physical basis for the coordinated optimization of membrane structure and interfacial properties.

works.title: Aromatic Peptide‐Enabled Cation‐π Engineering in Lamellar Nanochannels for Enhanced Cation Selectivity
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Ion selectivity is central to nanochannel membranes for ion separation, molecular recognition, and energy conversion. However, conventional membranes primarily rely on electrostatic repulsion to regulate ion selectivity; the short‐range and weak nature limits high selectivity. Herein, a cation‐π engineering strategy is proposed by intercalating aromatic peptides (APs) into sub‐nanometer graphene oxide (GO) channels. Systematic tuning of the π‐system with phenylalanine (F)‐, tyrosine (Y)‐, and tryptophan (W)‐based peptides reveals a dual role of cation‐π interactions, involving electrostatic attraction and cation confinement. Specifically, the Y‐based AP‐intercalated GO membrane achieves a cation transference number of 0.614, representing a 16.95% improvement over GO membrane, which is attributed to electrostatic attraction of π‐system toward cations. Significantly, experiments and simulations reveal a nonmonotonic relation between selectivity and π‐system density, excessive π‐system density strengthens confinement and compromises selectivity. Moreover, the W‐based AP‐intercalated GO membrane exhibits a maximum power density of 20.11 W/m 2 under a 50‐fold NaCl gradient through an optimized selectivity‐permeability balance. Notably, the power density is increased to 29.99 W/m 2 after introducing Mg 2+ , which competitively occupies indole π‐sites to facilitate Na + transport. This work uncovers the role of cation‐π interactions in confined channels, offering a chemical design principle for selective ion‐channel membranes.

works.title: Insights into Desalination Performance of Spacing-Tunable Laminated MXene Membranes via Molecular Dynamics and Machine Learning
works.abstract: Abstract Developing desalination membranes that combine high water permeance with high ion rejection remains important for freshwater production. Laminated MXene membranes are promising because their surface chemistry and channel dimensions are tunable, yet the respective roles of sheet-edge openings and interlayer spacing in staggered channels remain unclear. We performed molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of 242 O- and F-terminated Ti3C2 MXene membrane systems, varying the sheet-edge gap and interlayer spacing, d, from 6 to 16 Å. Machine learning (ML) analysis identified gap as the main structural variable governing water permeance and the extent of ion penetration, while d further regulated transport within the interlayer channels. Water and ion density distributions showed that gap primarily controlled entry into the laminated membrane, whereas d affected postentry transport and ion hydration. Na–Ow radial distribution functions and hydration-loss analyses indicated that narrow interlayer channels mainly perturbed the second hydration shell of Na+. Under matched geometries, surface termination produced weaker and more localized changes in water and ion distributions. These results distinguish entry control by the sheet-edge gap from postentry regulation by interlayer spacing and provide molecular guidance for designing spacing-tunable laminated MXene membranes.

works.title: Recovering Rare Earth Elements from Mining Effluent via Synergistic Angstrom-Scale Confinement and Phosphate-Mediated Coordination in MXene Membranes
institutions: University of Science and Technology of China
University of Science and Technology of China , , ,
Ganjiang Innovation Academy, Chinese Academy of Sciences , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Recovering rare earth elements (REEs) from complex aqueous streams is essential for advancing sustainable resource recovery but remains hindered by low REE concentrations and strong competition with impurity ions. Herein, we introduce a biomimetic MXene membrane that integrates phosphate-based molecular recognition with angstrom-level control of interlayer spacing to achieve the selective and continuous recovery of REEs from wastewaters. By intercalating aminophosphonic molecules within Ti3C2Tx layers, the membrane precisely tunes the nanochannel size and establishes coordinatively active oxygen sites that preferentially bind trivalent lanthanides under nanoconfinement. Such a design enables a synergistic mechanism in which steric exclusion and ligand–metal coordination coregulate ion transport, leading to markedly improved selectivity toward REE recovery. The optimized 2-AEP-M membrane exhibited a Ca2+/Dy3+ selectivity of 243.47 in simulated solutions and 130.69 in actual REE mining wastewater. After membrane separation and subsequent precipitation and calcination, REEs constituted 90.2% of the quantified cationic species in the recovered solid products. Experimental and computational analyses reveal that phosphate groups promote Dy3+ coordination, underpinning the observed ion discrimination. The membrane also demonstrates antiswelling stability and antibacterial properties, supporting its potential for long-term deployment. This work integrates chemical affinity with angstrom-confined transport, offering a platform for precise ion separation and sustainable REE recovery.

works.title: Divalent Cations and Chlorine Synergistically Reshape T6SS-Mediated Microbial Competition in Water Distribution System Biofilms
works.abstract: Abstract Microbial interactions shape the community structure and function in drinking water distribution system (DWDS) biofilms, yet how the dynamic competition is regulated in biofilms remains poorly understood. Here, we show that divalent cations (Ca2+, Mg2+) and chlorine in drinking water synergistically activate the type VI secretion system (T6SS) in opportunistic pathogens within biofilms. Field-collected biofilms serve as ecological hotspots that selectively enrich specific T6SS-harboring pathogens. Using simulated pipe systems and mutant validation, we further establish that divalent cations and chlorine enhance c-di-GMP signaling to promote T6SS-mediated colonization. This activation stimulates EPS production, whose polysaccharides mitigate T6SS attack, dampening the competitive advantage during mid-stage maturation but allowing gradual resurgence over extended succession. This divalent cation-chlorine-driven interplay shapes ecological succession, selectively retaining T6SS-proficient cells and establishing a “biofilm reservoir effect.” Under chlorine decay, T6SS-active pathogens can be released into bulk water, elevating exposure risks. Conversely, reducing divalent cations via nanofiltration suppresses T6SS across multiple pathogens, limiting reservoir accumulation and release. Our findings identify divalent cation availability as a key environmental signal associated with T6SS-mediated competition, linking water chemistry to pathogen persistence. This work suggests integrating membrane-based divalent cation removal with chlorine management as a chemistry-based strategy to mitigate microbial risks, advancing an integrated water quality paradigm for drinking water safety.

works.title: Fabrication of MIL-53(Al)-Incorporated Cellulose Acetate Mixed Matrix Forward Osmosis Membrane for Seawater Desalination
institutions: School of Water Conservancy and Environment, University of Jinan, Jinan 250022, China
works.abstract: Forward osmosis (FO) membranes have received growing attention in the field of water treatment. Nevertheless, their practical application in seawater desalination remains restricted, underscoring the imperative of developing advanced membrane modification techniques. In this study, we synthesized metal–organic framework MIL-53(Al) nanoparticles via a hydrothermal method and incorporated them into cellulose acetate (CA) membranes to fabricate a CA/MIL-53(Al) mixed-matrix FO membrane. The synthesized MIL-53(Al) nanoparticles were characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and N2 adsorption–desorption analysis. The effects of MIL-53(Al) loading, pore-forming agent content, mixing temperature, and coagulation bath temperature on the membrane performance were systematically investigated to optimize the fabrication conditions. Under the optimal conditions, the prepared CA/MIL-53(Al) mixed matrix FO membrane exhibited a water flux of 65.71 L/(m2·h) and a reverse salt flux of 2.20 g/(m2·h). Compared with the pristine CA FO membrane, the incorporation of MIL-53(Al) significantly improved the membrane permeability and separation performance. These enhancements were attributed to the improved hydrophilicity and optimized membrane structure induced by MIL-53(Al) nanoparticles. This study demonstrates that MIL-53(Al) is an effective nanofiller for the fabrication of high-performance CA-based FO membranes and provides a promising strategy for seawater desalination applications.

works.title: Unlocking feedforward capabilities in Model Predictive Control algorithms to deal with measurable disturbances
works.abstract: Disturbance rejection is a central objective in process control, particularly when measurable disturbances can be exploited through feedforward action. Although Model Predictive Control (MPC) naturally incorporates disturbance models and prediction capabilities, standard formulations cannot achieve complete disturbance rejection since the cost function penalises control effort. This limitation prevents MPC from reproducing the behaviour of classical feedforward compensators. This work proposes a novel framework to embed true feedforward capabilities within MPC without removing the control effort penalty. The approach introduces a dual-control structure in which two control actions are computed simultaneously: a tracking-oriented action addressing set-point tracking and robustness, and a feedforward-oriented action dedicated to disturbance rejection. Both contributions are combined into a single control signal on which the process constraints are explicitly enforced. The feedforward-oriented action is formulated without penalising control effort, enabling full compensation of measurable disturbances. The methodology is developed for Dynamic Matrix Control (DMC), Generalised Predictive Control (GPC), and state-space MPC. Its effectiveness is demonstrated through simulation studies, including comparisons with standard MPC and classical feedforward schemes. A case study based on a reverse osmosis process shows that the proposed approach improves disturbance rejection while preserving constraint handling and overall control performance.

works.title: Slippery Amphiphilic Antifouling Loose Nanofiltration Membrane with “Double-Defense” Functionalities for High-Salinity Organic Wastewater Sustainable Management
institutions: Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Environmental Pollution Control and Remediation Technology
Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Environmental Pollution Control and Remediation Technology , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Loose nanofiltration (LNF) holds potential for sustainable management of high-salinity organic wastewater through precise organics/salts fractionation, but practical application is constrained by severe organic–inorganic combined fouling. Herein, we propose a “double-defense” antifouling strategy and develop a slippery amphiphilic LNF membrane via facile stepwise surface modification. A hydrophilic branched polyethylenimine (PEI) network was first cross-linked onto a polyamide (PA) substrate to form a fouling-resistant protection layer, followed by covalent grafting of liquid-like polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) brushes to confer a slippery, fouling-release surface. The PEI layer acts as a hydration and electrostatic barrier to repel organic-cation complexes and scale precursors, while the slippery PDMS layer with high mobility and low surface energy minimizes interfacial interactions and strengthens hydraulic shear responsiveness. During the concentration of authentic leachate membrane bioreactor (MBR) effluent, the optimized membrane showed superior antifouling performance: low flux decline ratio (FDR) of 41.6% and high flux recovery ratio (FRR) of 98.1%, outperforming a commercial PA membrane (FDR 91.2%, FRR 78.4%). It also delivered an organics/salts fractionation selectivity 7.8 times that of the commercial membrane, demonstrating multiple cycles stability. This rationally designed architecture offers a practical solution for challenging wastewater and is extensible to other PA-based membrane systems in environmental applications.

works.title: Surface‐Coordinated Gas–Solid Polymerization Enables Quasi‐2D Polyphenylacetylene Single‐Crystalline Nanoribbons
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Functional Crystals and Devices Fujian Institute of Research on the Structure of Matter Chinese Academy of Sciences Fuzhou Fujian P. R. China
Fujian Science & Technology Innovation Laboratory for Optoelectronic Information of China Fuzhou Fujian P. R. China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional (2D) conjugated polymer single crystals are highly desirable for optoelectronics, yet their realization is limited by the intrinsic coupling between molecular‐weight buildup and chain entanglement, which disrupts long‐range order. Here, we report a gas–solid interfacial polymerization strategy that decouples monomer diffusion from chain propagation, enabling the growth of quasi‐2D polyphenylacetylene (PPA) single‐crystalline nanoribbons on Cu/CuO x surfaces. This process is likely enabled by surface coordination‐assisted activation of phenylacetylene and directional π‐stacking‐driven assembly, which suppress chain entanglement and promote crystallographic ordering. As a result, micrometer‐scale PPA single‐crystalline nanoribbons with left‐handed cis‐transoidal helical chains and long‐range crystallinity are obtained. Under an ideal fully extended‐chain model, the PPA chains exhibit a geometrically estimated upper‐bound molecular weight of up to ∼3.7 × 10 9 g mol − 1 . The resulting PPA nanoribbons exhibit efficient charge transport and broadband photodetection from 375 to 1550 nm, with a responsivity of 30.1 A W − 1 and a detectivity of 8.65 × 10 1 2 Jones. This interfacial synthesis strategy provides a route to overcoming the trade‐off between molecular‐weight buildup and structural order in conjugated polymers, offering opportunities for quasi‐2D polymer semiconductors in flexible optoelectronics and programmable chiral materials.

works.title: Theoretical Calculations of CO2/CH4 Separation through Windowed Carbon Nanotube Membranes
works.abstract: Abstract Distinct topological features endow windowed carbon nanotube (CNT) membranes with great potential as molecular sieves for efficient gas separation and purification. In this work, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were adopted to systematically investigate the CO2/CH4 selective separation performance of such membranes. Key structural and operational parameters, including CNT diameter, pressure, initial feed gas molar ratio, and nanowindow density, were modulated to comprehensively evaluate the molecular sieving capacity toward CO2 and CH4. Simulation results reveal that heteroatom-functionalized windowed CNT membranes exhibit outstanding CO2 permselectivity and superior CH4 purification capacity, with a maximum CO2/CH4 separation selectivity of 41. Among all simulated configurations, the 4N5F-modified nanowindow CNT membrane exhibits the optimal separation performance, yielding a CO2 capture fraction of 0.77 and recovered CH4 purity of 97.6%. Such excellent molecular sieving performance confirms that windowed CNT membranes hold promising prospects for direct CO2 capture and raw shale gas purification.

works.title: Recent Advances in Polybenzimidazole-Based Membrane for Flow Batteries
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Organic-Inorganic Composite Materials
School of Materials Science and Engineering, Dalian Jiaotong University , Dalian 116028 ,

State Key Laboratory of Organic-Inorganic Composites, Beijing Key Laboratory of Intelligent Design and Manufacturing for Hydrogen Energy Materials, College of Chemical Engineering, Beijing University of Chemical Technology, Beijing 100029 ,
works.abstract: Abstract Polybenzimidazole (PBI)-based membranes are promising for flow batteries (FB) due to their excellent ion selectivity, thermal stability, and tunable ion conductivity. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in PBI-based membranes for various flow battery systems, categorized by fabrication method and membrane type. First, the effects of solvent evaporation-induced phase inversion (EIPS), water-induced phase inversion (NIPS), vapor-induced phase inversion (VIPS), and mixed-phase inversion on membrane structure and performance are summarized. Second, based on membrane type, the ion conduction mechanisms and performance differences of dense membranes, porous membranes, and blend membranes are discussed separately.Third, applications and challenges of PBI-based membranes in vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFB), zinc-based flow batteries (ZRFB) and iron-based flow batteries (IRFB) are discussed. Finally, structure-property relationships are summarized, and design strategies for high-performance PBI membranes are proposed. Nevertheless, PBI based membranes still face critical bottlenecks for real world RFB applications. Their ionic conductivity strongly relies on acid base doping, and irreversible dopant loss during continuous electrolyte circulation would induce progressive performance decay over cycling. This review provides a systematic reference for the rational design and application of PBI-based membranes in flow batteries.

works.title: Explainable machine learning framework for design and performance optimization of MOF-TFN FO membranes
institutions: North China University of Science and Technology
works.abstract: The escalating need for efficient and sustainable water-treatment solutions has placed MOF-incorporated TFN FO membranes at the forefront of membrane research thanks to their notable potential for seawater desalination and wastewater treatment, largely due to their capacity for high Water Flux (Jw) coupled with suppressed Reverse Solute Flux (Js). Still, a persistent and often frustrating challenge lies in navigating the inherent trade-off between Jw and Js. In this study, we turn to machine learning (ML) for a more systematic membrane design and performance optimization strategy. Beyond prediction, we sought to open the “black box” and understand why certain membrane compositions and operating conditions lead to better outcomes. Through Pearson correlation analysis, SHAP-based feature importance, single- and two-variable PDPs, DML causal-effect heterogeneity analysis, and feature-guided uncertainty-aware stepwise PSO we identified not only which structural and operational parameters matter most, but also how they interact—sometimes in non-intuitive ways. The main contribution of this study lies in integrating all these techniques into a complete ML framework, which not only delivers robust, data-driven performance predictions for MOF-TFN FO membranes, but also provides actionable guidance for their design and optimization, reinforcing the value of ML as a tool for innovation in membrane technology

works.title: An integrated pervaporation-dia-nanofiltration process for aroma recovery and ethanol removal in white wine
works.abstract: Membrane technologies are widely used in ethanol removal from wine (DW); however, they face challenges in maintaining wine quality, particularly in retaining volatile compounds. This study evaluated for the first time a two-stage membrane process (PV-NF) combining pervaporation (PV) and dia-nanofiltration (dia-NF) to produce a white dealcoholized wine-based beverages (DW; ethanol <0.5% v /v) with aroma preservation. PV was first used to extract and recover aroma compounds from the original wine (OW). The resulting dearomatized wine underwent dia-NF for ethanol removal, after which the recovered aroma concentrate was reconstituted into the final DW, ensuring its alcohol content did not exceed 0.5% v /v. Additionally, the physicochemical, color, and volatile profiles of the produced DWs were studied. The results indicated that total acidity and volatile acidity were reduced by 80–82% and 35–52%, respectively. Furthermore, reducing sugars, glycerin, malic acid, and tartaric acid experienced partial depletion, while citric acid was completely lost. Color profiles were also impacted; the extended processing time of the combined PV-NF approach, elevating the browning index (Abs 420 nm) to as high as 0.71 AU compared to the OW (0.07 AU). The PV-NF process successfully produced DW with ethanol content below 0.5% v /v while retaining 27–31% of total aroma compounds, outperforming NF alone (6–9% retention). These findings highlight the potential of combining PV-NF to mitigate volatile losses during the process and stress the need for optimizing processing strategies to balance ethanol reduction with sensory integrity.

works.title: Lithium–Magnesium Separation in Salt Lake Brine Using Electrodialysis: A Multi‐Physical Modeling With Neural‐Network Prediction
institutions: School of Energy and Power Engineering Xi'an Jiaotong University Xi'an Shaanxi China
Department of Electronics and Communications Engineering Capital University Cairo Egypt
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium resource serves as critical material for lithium‐ion battery industry, and it becomes indispensable for global technological progress and economic development. Facing the challenge of high magnesium‐to‐lithium ratio in salt lake brines of China, electrodialysis (ED) exhibits great potential as an extraction technology. However, lithium–magnesium separation using ED is a complicated multi‐physical process, and insufficient understanding of lithium extraction mechanism limits its efficiency improvement. Hence, the current work constructs a multi‐physical model for lithium extraction from high magnesium salt lake brine using ED to reveal ion migration behavior and separation mechanism under synergistic fields. On the basis of a parametric analysis with optimization, the magnesium‐to‐lithium ratio in brine is dramatically decreased from initial state at 105.05 to 1.87 at the outlet of ED device under the temperature of 323.15 K, potential difference of 0.5 V, and membrane thickness of 0.35 mm. Furthermore, five neural‐network models are developed as surrogates of the multi‐physical model using 2784 simulation‐generated samples without experimental data. Multidimensional dilated convolutional neural network (MDCNN) achieves the lowest in‐domain mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.0293%, 0.0395%, and 0.7735%, respectively, whereas R 2 (>0.998) provides limited discrimination. In 24 additional out‐of‐domain simulation cases, MDCNN achieves the lowest MAPE (3.8846%), whereas convolutional attention neural network (CNN‐Attention) achieves the lowest RMSE (0.2525) and the highest R 2 (0.9494), demonstrating complementary generalization strengths. The current work offers a theoretical basis for optimizing lithium–magnesium separation performance using ED with neural‐network surrogate modeling, laying foundation for big data analysis and development of experimental correlations.

works.title: Mechanisms of Magnesium Transport Through Cell Membranes: The Primacy of the Free Divalent Cation and Implications for Magnesium Supplementation
institutions: IPEV Institute for Prevention and Nutrition, 85737 Ismaning, Germany
Department of Radiotherapy and Radiation Oncology, Franziskus Hospital Bielefeld, 33615 Bielefeld, Germany
Biomedical Centre Martin, Jessenius Faculty of Medicine in Martin, Comenius University in Bratislava, 03601 Martin, Slovakia
works.abstract: Magnesium (Mg2+) is the second most abundant intracellular cation and an essential cofactor for more than 600 enzymatic reactions. Commercial claims that particular magnesium salts preferentially deliver magnesium to the brain, heart or muscle raise a mechanistic question: do established transport pathways support selective delivery of an intact magnesium complex? This narrative review examines the dissolution of magnesium salts in the gastrointestinal tract, paracellular and transcellular intestinal absorption, plasma magnesium speciation, the transport and regulatory proteins involved in cellular magnesium handling, and selected formulation-comparison studies. Magnesium is absorbed as the free divalent cation Mg2+, and the anion of an ingested salt is handled independently. In plasma, approximately 55% of magnesium is ionised, 30% is bound to albumin and 15% is complexed with small anions. All characterised magnesium transport proteins, including TRPM6, TRPM7, SLC41A1, CNNM proteins, MagT1 and MRS2, handle the free Mg2+ ion. The literature reviewed does not establish a pathway that recognises an ingested magnesium–ligand complex and delivers it selectively to a particular organ. Supplements may nevertheless differ in dissolution, gastrointestinal tolerability, systemic exposure and independent effects of the anion. Claims of organ-specific magnesium delivery based on salt form therefore lack a demonstrated mechanistic basis.

works.title: 3D Solar‐Driven Interfacial Evaporator Based on Tailored TiO <sub>2</sub> Nanotube Arrays by Wireless Anodizing for Efficient Desalination
institutions: College of Ocean Science and Engineering Shanghai Maritime University Shanghai People's Republic of China
Merchant Marine College Shanghai Maritime University Shanghai People's Republic of China
Shanghai Ship and Shipping Research Institute Co., LTD. Shanghai People's Republic of China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation is an energy‐efficient desalination strategy. However, the existing solar‐driven interfacial evaporators mostly rely on a surface‐localized photothermal layer for heat confinement, which limits evaporation exclusively to the top surface. The internal transfer channels and potential evaporation area remain unexplored, restricting water production rates. Here, a wireless anodization with a composite bipolar electrode has been proposed to prepare completely internal anodized porous Ti with TiO 2 nanotube (TNT) arrays, serving for 3D solar‐driven interfacial evaporation. By regulating the reaction area and intensity, the TiO 2 nanotubes (TNTs) with tailored size (diameter of 120–170 nm, length of 3–10 µm) have successfully anisotropically grown on the porous Ti substrates, constructing internal interconnected channels. The obtained wireless anodized porous Ti (WAPT) possessed an increased surface area of 7.938 m 2 ·g −1 , as well as solar absorbance >80%, superhydrophilicity (totally wetting within 10 s), and low evaporation enthalpy (451.83 kJ·kg −1 ), making efficient water evaporation with larger evaporation area and lower energy consumption possible. Under one‐sun irradiation, the WAPT showed an evaporation rate of 1.68 kg·m −2 ·h −1 with no salt crystallization and could maintain over 30 days. By assembling the WAPTs into a 3D interfacial evaporator, cooperated with wind‐driven cold evaporation, the maximum evaporation rate reached 2.412 kg·m −2 ·h −1 . In outdoor conditions (solar intensity of 0.6 kW·m −2 at 12 pm), the water collection rate reached 1.59 kg·m −2 ·h −1 . This work should make possible the development of a high‐performance solar‐driven interfacial evaporator for various applications.

works.title: Buried Reed Barrier Layers for Sustainable Desalination of Coastal Saline Soils
institutions: College of Water Conservancy and Civil Engineering, Shandong Agricultural University, Tai’an 271018, China
works.abstract: Soil salinization poses severe threats to agricultural production and ecological sustainability in the Yellow River Delta of China. Conventional porous barrier materials such as straw, river sand and construction waste have unavoidable limitations in raw-material supply and environmental safety. This study explored the potential of Phragmites australis segments as an eco-friendly, locally available porous barrier layer for sustainable coastal saline-soil remediation. Laboratory soil column simulation tests were carried out with four reed-segment length treatments (2 cm, 5 cm, 8 cm, 11 cm) and a reed-free control (CK) to investigate soil percolation and drainage, vertical salt content distribution and layered desalination rate. Buried reed segments significantly enhanced percolation and drainage under leaching, with the 5 cm treatment performing best. After leaching, soil salt content increased monotonically with depth in all treatments, and CK retained significantly higher salt contents than the reed-amended treatments throughout the profile. Reed-segment length exerted slight effects on topsoil desalination but significant effects on deep soil layers. All reed treatments achieved higher desalination rates than CK. The 5 cm treatment yielded stable salt-mass-weighted profile desalination rates of 96.59%, 96.76% and 97.15% at 24 h, 84 h and 168 h, respectively, showing optimal performance under laboratory soil-column conditions. These findings provide a sustainable, low-cost technical reference for the ecological amelioration of coastal saline soils.

works.title: Ligand-engineered layered solid–liquid interfaces enable fast and selective ion transport
works.abstract: Abstract Ion transport behaviors are central to ion separation, micro-/nano-fluidics, and interfacial catalysis, yet achieving high ion transport rate and selectivity remains challenging in nonaqueous systems. Here, we propose a unique solid–liquid cooperative interface built from a layered cyano-bridged metal framework (CMF) and nonaqueous solvents to simultaneously increase cation (Li+) conductivity (9.5 mS·cm−1) and transport selectivity (~ 0.9). Mechanistic analysis based on theoretical calculations, supported by electrochemical measurements, shows that the nonaqueous solvents can work as functional interfacial ligands at the surface of layered CMFs, including outer-layer solvent ligands (OSLs) and interlayer solvent ligands (ISLs), which can restructure the interfacial Li+ migration environment and salt speciation. It is found that OSLs with higher polarity symmetry would interact more strongly with the unsaturated metal sites on the CMF’s surface, thereby promoting coordination competition at the interface, accelerating solvation-renewal dynamics, and increasing the Li+ transport rate. ISLs with higher polarity symmetry could stabilize a low-curvature surface of CMF, strengthen anion anchoring at the unsaturated metal sites, increase selectivity for Li+ transport, and further improve overall Li+ transport rate. Therefore, we provide a potential strategy to construct a unique solid–liquid interface using CMF solids and rationally designed interfacial solvent ligands to promote the ion transport behaviors.

works.title: Data-driven well-resolved aggregate-capacity screening for brackish-blending management in Kuwait under pumping and total-dissolved-solids constraints
works.abstract: Brackish groundwater is a strategic supply buffer for arid states reliant on energy-intensive seawater desalination, yet the operational condition of legacy well fields and the distribution-side limits on dispatchable volume remain understudied. Both are addressed here for Kuwait, where desalination supplies ∼ 92% of municipal water. A ministry-level record of 393 wells across five production fields was assembled, and a well-resolved screening linear program was formulated to maximize brackish blending subject to the 1,000-ppm upper total-dissolved-solids (TDS) limit of the applicable Gulf drinking-water standard and an aggregate pumping bound. The model resolves individual wells but represents the distribution side as a single aggregate capacity scalar; it is a screening model, not a hydraulic network model, and its optimum is an upper bound on what a station-resolved network could deliver. Current operations support 62.24MIGD of blending; all rehabilitation scenarios saturate the pumping bound at 90.70MIGD, a 1.46 × (45.7%) uplift. The binding constraint is, therefore, distribution-side aggregate capacity, not upstream well availability. This finding is robust: a zone-partitioned re-solve yields 87.8 MIGD–90.70MIGD, and crediting the standby reserve shifts the binding constraint to the TDS limit; well availability never binds. Constraining dispatch to the nine documented pumping stations reduces the realizable volume to 55.08 MIGD (61% of the aggregate optimum) when each field feeds a single station, quantifying the cost of the full-connectivity assumption; the binding constraint stays on the distribution side in every case. A lexicographic formulation returns the same volume at lower delivered TDS, yielding a unique dispatch portfolio. The S0 → S3 transition increases the TDS-feasible substitution ceiling by 45.7% (a theoretical upper bound under cogeneration coupling), supporting SDG 6 targets 6.4 and 6.5. The TDS volumes reported represent TDS-feasible blending maximums for the distribution system and do not independently determine that the blended product will be safe for consumption. This diagnostic (i.e., comparing the rehabilitation well flow rates with the production flow rate of the existing firm distribution system) can also be applied to other arid-state utilities.

works.title: Seawater Desalination in the Middle East and North Africa: Environmental Impacts of Brine Discharge, Energy Use and Pathways to Sustainable Expansion in Egypt
works.abstract: Desalination has become indispensable to water security in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), which produces almost half of the world's desalinated water. Egypt, facing a widening gap between Nile supply and demand, plans to expand seawater desalination from about 1.2–1.4 million m³ per day today to several million m³ per day within a decade. This review synthesises evidence on the environmental impacts of desalination, with emphasis on brine discharge, chemical additives, intake effects and energy use, and on management options relevant to Egypt's Mediterranean and Red Sea coasts. Globally, about 15,900 plants produce some 95 million m³ per day of fresh water and about 142 million m³ per day of brine, of which about 70% is produced in MENA. Brine, typically with roughly twice the salinity of seawater and containing antiscalants, coagulants and cleaning chemicals, can form dense plumes that affect seagrasses, corals and benthic communities near outfalls, particularly in poorly flushed embayments. Intakes cause impingement and entrainment of marine organisms, and energy use, still dominated by fossil fuels, generates substantial greenhouse-gas emissions. The review shows that most impacts can be reduced through careful site selection, subsurface intakes, diffuser outfalls, environmental monitoring, renewable energy and emerging brine-valorisation technologies, and proposes guidelines for Egypt's expansion, particularly to protect the Red Sea's coral reefs.

works.title: Upcycling waste polyester into cobalt-molybdenum sulfide-decorated carbon foam for photothermal desalination and parametric optimization using Taguchi design of experiments
works.abstract: Photothermal desalination is an emerging solar-powered technique for water desalination. One of the primary open issues in the field is the development of new materials that guarantee high photothermal efficiency and evaporation rates. In this study, waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles are upcycled into carbon foam, which is then decorated with Co-Mo2S3 via hydrothermal synthesis to prepare a photothermal evaporator. The as-synthesized Co-Mo2S3/carbon foam (CF) achieved an average evaporation rate of 2.13 kg m-2 h-1 during a 1-h experiment under 1,000 W m-2 irradiation using a 3.5% NaCl solution, compared to 1.55 kg m-2 h-1 obtained for CF. A Taguchi orthogonal-array design of experiments (DOE) was used to optimize the effect of input parameters on the evaporation rate of saline water. The experimental design matrix shows a maximum water evaporation rate of 1.77 kg m-2 h-1 under real sunlight. Taguchi analysis presents the optimal operating parameters for the evaporation rate as follows: salinity 30 g L-1 (level 1), saline water pH 5 (level 2), and time 2 h (level 2). The statistical outcomes show that salinity is the main factor affecting the evaporation rate. This study addresses water scarcity and promotes the circular economy by transforming plastic waste into a valuable resource for producing clean water and provides deeper insight into the optimization of the operating parameters using statistical tools.

works.title: Boronic acid-functionalized graphene aerogels for selective catechol removal in complex multicomponent phenolic aerosols
institutions: China Tobacco Yunnan Industrial Co., Ltd. (China)
Kunming University of Science and Technology
works.abstract: Selective adsorption in complex multicomponent aerosols remains challenging because structurally similar molecules often compete for identical adsorption sites. Herein, a boronic acid-functionalized three-dimensional graphene aerogel was developed as a selective adsorbent for phenolic compounds. Following 1,2-benzenediboronic acid modification, the specific surface area of graphene aerogel increased from 380.69 to 539.88 m 2 g −1 . In dynamic multicomponent aerosol experiments, the detected catechol amounts after filtration through B-14/CA and B-18/CA were 65.94 and 65.21 μg/cig, respectively, compared with 106.13 μg/cig for the conventional cellulose acetate filter. Other representative phenolic compounds exhibited responses distinct from that of catechol, demonstrating differential filtration in the competitive system. Density functional theory calculations showed that the optimized catechol complex did not correspond to a conventional boronate ester. Instead, a noncovalent B···O contact of approximately 2.06 Å closed a seven-membered pseudo-cyclic adsorption configuration without dehydration. The similar adsorption energies of catechol and guaiacol, −0.34319 and −0.34799 eV, respectively, indicated that a single optimized adsorption energy was insufficient to explain the experimental difference. These results suggest that the combination of hierarchical porous transport and configuration-dependent noncovalent recognition contributes to preferential catechol retention in multicomponent aerosols.

works.title: Probing Adsorbed Water in Al(HCOO)3 Metal–Organic Framework by Multinuclear and Multidimensional Solid-State NMR Spectroscopy
institutions: Center of High Field NMR Spectroscopy and Imaging, Nanyang Technological University, 21 Nanyang Link, Singapore 637371, Singapore
Tianjin Key Lab for Rare Earth Materials and Applications, School of Materials Science and Engineering, Nankai University, Tianjin 300350, China
works.abstract: Water affects the local structure, dynamics, and adsorption properties of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), yet the molecular-level characterization of confined water remains difficult due to the lack of long-range ordering. Here, we study the water adsorption in microporous MOF Al(HCOO)3 using multinuclear solid-state NMR spectroscopy combined with ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. 1H NMR resolves two distinct confined-water environments and reveals water–framework and water–water contacts. 13C and 27Al NMR further show that water adsorption perturbs the local environments of the formate linkers and AlO6 coordination units. Powder X-ray diffraction shows that the long-range crystalline framework is preserved after water loading, whereas 13C NMR detects a minor mobile formate-containing species that disappears upon re-dehydration, consistent with the partial local hydrolysis of the framework. 2H NMR distinguishes both highly mobile and confined water undergoing rapid anisotropic reorientation. The effective quadrupolar line shape is consistent with rapid anisotropic reorientation, for which C2-axis flips provide one possible motional model. 1H–2H CP-HETCOR NMR further suggests dipolar contacts between restricted water molecules, the formate framework, and neighboring water molecules. AIMD simulations support water–framework interactions associated with the two pore environments and the formation of an interconnected water network. These results provide molecular-level insights into the water adsorption sites and dynamics in Al(HCOO)3 and the previously unreported partial hydrolysis of this MOF.

works.title: Stacking-Controlled Reactivity and Friction of Water in Atomic-Scale hBN Channels from First Principles
works.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
works.abstract: Abstract Understanding the behavior of water confined in atomic-scale channels is a cornerstone of nanoscience and nanofluidics. Unlike graphene, isostructural hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) spontaneously acquires electric charges in liquid water due to hydroxide ion (OH–) adsorption. Yet, whether this reactivity persists under monolayer and bilayer confinement remains an open question. Here, we use first-principles modeling to uncover the role of stacking symmetry (AA vs AA’) between hBN walls─a factor that has so far received little attention in boron nitride systems─on the structural and dynamical properties of Å-scale water. We systematically probe neutral, alkaline, and acidic environments to elucidate how water self-ions (H3O+ and OH–) interact with hBN interfaces. Combining ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations with machine learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) for extended time scales, we obtain a consistent description, at the revPBE-D3 level of theory, of water’s structural and transport properties under extreme confinement. Our results demonstrate that stacking symmetry critically impacts monolayer water systems and modulates the energetics of chemisorbed hydroxide and interfacial friction. In alkaline conditions, chemisorbed hydroxide doubles friction, yet its effect on water diffusion is minimal. Strikingly, monolayer water exhibits a twofold diffusion enhancement compared to bilayer water, reaching bulk-like values─revealing that diffusion is an intrinsic property of the water layer, independent of wall chemistry. This work delivers quantitative estimates of friction and diffusion coefficients, conditional on the chosen functional and water loadings, that provide a reference for future experiments on Å-scale water transport.
